replacement.title: Recover behind the puck-side handoff
replacement.objective: Track the second attacker after a puck-side handoff and keep the net-side lane in view.
replacement.briefing: Gold attacks Navy’s left net. Gold 1 carries in a wide lane and is already closer to the net than D1. Gold 2 is inside support. YOU are recovering from farther up ice. In this exercise D1 tries to recover toward the carrier while YOU account for Gold 2; no coverage or arrival time is guaranteed.
cues: Gold 1 controls the puck and is closer to Navy’s net than D1.
Gold 2 is the inside support attacker.
YOU are still recovering; C is another Navy player.

questions.prompt: What makes a recovery call useful after a puck-side handoff?
questions.explanation: Name the carrier, inside support and intended recovery responsibility. Keep scanning and updating with D1; a call does not prove either threat is covered.

replacement.objective: Use a changing forecheck to select a reachable teammate and preserve a reset connection.

Whether F1 or D2 is reachable
The board side decides the pass by itself

Compare F1 and D2
Carry or pass, then check the next lane

questions.prompt: Why should YOU compare passing angles as well as distance from the boards?
questions.explanation: An angle can keep the puck carrier connected to both D2 and F1 while showing the forecheck. If one route closes, the other remains a live branch only when reachable.

replacement.objective: Coordinate a behind-net exchange by naming the puck carrier, inside threat and teammate cover.
replacement.briefing: Gold attacks Navy’s left net. Gold 1 controls the puck behind that net. YOU and D2 are on opposite sides. C is assigned to account for Gold 2 near the slot, but C starts farther from the net than Gold 2. Coordinate pressure and slot coverage as Gold 1 changes sides.

questions.prompt: Which Navy forward controls the puck behind Gold’s goal line?

options.text: F1
F2
YOU

questions.explanation: F1 controls the puck behind the attacking goal line.

questions.prompt: Which two details support a high outlet?

options.text: Whether F1 can reach a high support option
Gold 1's slot coverage
Following F2 into the same low space

questions.explanation: Carrier visibility and the slot defender shape the value of a separated high outlet.

questions.prompt: Arrange a high-outlet read.

options.text: Locate F1, F2 and the slot defender
Offer a separated high lane
Re-check the carrier and point-side pressure

questions.explanation: The outlet remains useful only when the carrier and pressure can connect to it.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a high support point separate from F2.
questions.explanation: The example stays nearer the blue line than F1 and F2. It moves farther from Gold 2 but nearer Gold 1, so recheck both before asking for a pass.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 leaves the slot to pressure the puck. What should YOU weigh?

options.text: An inside connection if F1 can reach it, or hold high if Gold 2 covers
Drop beside F2 without checking the slot
Shoot because the slot defender moved

questions.explanation: Gold 1 leaving can open an inside branch, but F1’s passing route and Gold 2’s coverage still need a scan.

questions.prompt: How does a high outlet help a low cycle?
questions.explanation: It gives F1 a separated option and can make Gold choose between the slot and the carrier. If the route is covered, remain available or reset instead of crowding F2.

questions.prompt: Which Navy player is the net-front reference?

options.text: F1
F2
Gold 1

questions.explanation: F1 is the Navy player positioned near the net-front lane.

questions.prompt: Which two checks shape the point decision?

options.text: Whether F1 could provide a useful screen
Whether F2 is reachable across the slot
The point role alone chooses the release without a lane check

questions.explanation: Compare the actual goalie view, traffic and route to F2. A net-front position alone does not establish a screen.

questions.prompt: Arrange a changed-lane point read.

options.text: Check Gold 1 and F1
Compare the release with F2
Re-check the net-side lane

questions.explanation: Check the defender, net-front traffic and F2 as part of a continuing scan. Recheck the lane before release; this is one suggested order.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare another shooting angle toward the net.
questions.explanation: The example changes the line toward the net and moves YOU closer to Gold 1. Recheck pressure, F1 and F2; a screen is not guaranteed.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 moves away and F1 leaves the net front, what deserves attention?

options.text: Compare F2 with the changed shot and traffic picture
Release through the former lane before checking F1’s screen
Assume the lane is still fully screened without rechecking

questions.explanation: The defender and screen both changed, so the next choice depends on the new support picture.

questions.prompt: What makes feedback on a point release useful in this rep?
questions.explanation: Name Gold 1, F1 and F2 and explain the shot, pass or protection options. Check the actual goalie and traffic before describing a useful screen.
